claims.text: The authoritative measurement of this trip is the GPS trace, not the bill. EV-GPS-00113 is an unimpaired 217-fix trace at a 10-second cadence with 100% coverage, no gaps and a longest gap of 0 seconds, and it records trace_distance_km of 20.18 km over the run from the 18:47:10 start to the 19:23:10 end. EV-FARE-00113 bills distance_charged_km of 20.2 km on the same run. Under POL-RD-01 the trace polyline figure governs the excess test and the rounded actual_distance_km on the trip record may not be cited for it, so the excess at issue can be no larger than 20.18 km less the correct baseline.

The baseline is the matched-itinerary optimal, not the solo optimal. TRP-00113 is a RYDE_POOL trip, and POL-RD-12 fixes the POL-RD-01 baseline at trip_record.optimal_distance_km of 19.40 km - the pooled route quoted at match time 18:42 for Punggol to the Hougang co-rider pickup to Raffles Place - and says in terms that a claim measured against solo_optimal_distance_km has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone. The 15.80 km solo figure in the claim text is carried for reference only. The rider accepts that distance attributable to a platform-matched co-rider collection is not a deviation, so the only excess properly at issue is what exceeds 19.40 km.

On the governing figures the excess is 0.78 km and 4.02% - the 20.18 km trace against the 19.40 km matched-itinerary baseline - which passes neither limb of the POL-RD-01 gate, since it is neither greater than 0.8 km nor greater than 20%, and the rider does not ask the tribunal to find a deviation the arithmetic does not support. The rider's point on this claim is a measurement point only: the excess must be taken from the trace's 20.18 km and must not be inflated to the rounded 20.2 km on the fare line or to the 15.80 km solo figure.

No exculpatory clause other than POL-RD-12 is open to the driver on this record, so the remaining excess beyond the matched itinerary is unexplained by any clause he can invoke. EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING, carries no payload and has an admissibility weight of 0.0 - the impairment is disclosed here as POL-GEN-02 requires - so there is no traffic advisory naming the Punggol, Hougang or CTE corridor in the 18:41-19:23 window and no POL-RD-03 closure exoneration is available. The three messages in EV-CHAT-00113 contain no rider instruction to detour and every waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04 cannot be run on this record. The trip_record shows no amended pickup or dropoff and no amended optimal distance, so POL-RD-05 has nothing to re-quote.

The rider's profile may not be used to load her claim. EV-RPROF-00113 records deviation_claims_60d of 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0, far below the four unsubstantiated claims POL-RD-08 requires before a sub-30% claim must be corroborated beyond the trace, so no enhanced corroboration burden attaches to this rider; and under POL-GEN-01 every other field on that profile - prior_disputes_filed, prior_no_show_flags, rating and the rest - is context only and cannot ground an adverse finding against her.

claims.text: The baseline for this trip is the matched pooled itinerary, not the rider's solo distance. trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_POOL, so under POL-RD-12 the POL-RD-01 optimal is trip_record.optimal_distance_km of 19.40 km. The governing actual figure is the GPS trace: derived.deviation.trace_distance_km is 20.18 km, giving an excess of 0.78 km, or 4.02% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 20% of optimal (3.88 km) AND 0.8 km absolute. 0.78 km clears neither limb and misses the absolute limb by 20 metres. No deviation is established, and under POL-RD-01 the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

The rider's 15.8 km figure is trip_record.solo_optimal_distance_km, carried on the record for reference only. Under POL-RD-12 a claim that measures excess against solo_optimal_distance_km has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone. The 4.4 km shortfall the claim_text asserts (20.2 minus 15.8) is an artefact of that mis-citation, not of anything the driver did. Both figures are on EV-TRIP-00113 and the ruling should name them side by side so it is visible why the arithmetic changes.

The detour the rider complains of — 'the driver went off to Hougang' — is the matched co-rider pickup, and POL-RD-12 excludes it by name: distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary is never a deviation and is removed from excess before POL-RD-01 is applied. The trace shows the vehicle stationary at Hougang Central for the boarding stop, consistent with a pick-up rather than a wander.

The rider was on notice before the wheels turned, so this is not a case of a route being altered behind his back. The platform's own match notification MSG-00113-001, sent 18:42:04, states 'Your pooled route now includes one pickup at Hougang Central before your drop-off. Estimated 19.4 km, 34 min'; the log records it read at 18:42:31, and the trip did not start until 18:47:10. The 19.4 km matched-itinerary figure on the trip record is the same figure the rider was quoted in the app.

The driver's counterparty statement is corroborated rather than contradicted by the platform's own records: he says a second passenger was matched at Hougang and that he drove the app route, and the system notification MSG-00113-001 records that match, MSG-00113-003 records his contemporaneous explanation 'pool booking, picking up the other passenger, app route', and the trace shows the stop. Nothing in the admitted evidence shows the vehicle anywhere the matched pooled itinerary did not put it.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. The trace here is unimpaired: 217 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 and a 10 s sampling interval — so there is no gap, jump or sampling defect under POL-RD-07. What that clean trace shows is 0.78 km and 4.02%. The threshold is not met, the burden never shifts to the driver, and no exculpatory clause need be invoked to defeat the claim.

No driver_profile check is engaged on this trip. POL-RD-06 is consulted only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation, and a 0.78 km excess is far below the 8.0 km / 50% material gate. In any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 471, so there is no repeat-deviation pattern, no POL-RD-06(b) FULL_REFUND uplift is available, and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is justified.

No traffic advisory covers the Punggol, Hougang or CTE corridors in this window — EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING and carries weight 0.0 — and the driver does not need one. The exoneration relied on is POL-RD-12, the platform's own matched pooled-itinerary baseline, not POL-RD-03. No closure is asserted, so the absence of an advisory costs this defence nothing; it is cited only so the absence is on the record.

There is no billing-integrity defect to refund under POL-RD-09(4). The fare breakdown is METERED on rate card RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDEPOOL, its line items reconcile, distance_charged_km of 20.2 matches the 20.18 km the trace records, erp_gantries is empty and airport_surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and a 3.00 pool discount was applied in the rider's favour. Every dollar charged traces to a line the rider actually consumed.

The disputed charge still stands: fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. The dispute is rider-filed, so NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03 is party-relative and preserves that present state — on this record the $6.00 contested stays with the driver. The driver drove the pooled itinerary the platform matched for him and quoted to the rider; the evidence does not support a refund against him, and it should not be invented to produce one.

ruling.explanation: Both sides ultimately agree on the arithmetic, and the records confirm it. This was a RYDE_POOL booking (TRP-00113, EV-TRIP-00113), so under POL-RD-12 the correct baseline is the matched pooled-itinerary distance of 19.40 km stored on the trip record at match time, not the 15.80 km solo figure. The app told you this before the wheels turned: at 18:42:04 the platform's own notification (MSG-00113-001, read 18:42:31) said 'Your pooled route now includes one pickup at Hougang Central before your drop-off. Estimated 19.4 km, 34 min', and the trip did not start until 18:47:10. The 15.80 km in the filing is trip_record.solo_optimal_distance_km, carried for reference only, and a claim measured against it fails on that ground alone. The governing actual distance is the GPS trace, not the bill: EV-GPS-00113 (weight 1.0) is unimpaired — 217 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, 10-second cadence — and records trace_distance_km of 20.18 km. Excess is 20.18 − 19.40 = 0.78 km, or 4.02% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed both 20% (3.88 km) and 0.8 km absolute; 0.78 km fails both and misses the absolute limb by about 20 metres. No deviation is established and no refund runs. The Hougang stop is the platform-matched co-rider pickup, which POL-RD-12 excludes from excess by name; the driver drove the itinerary he was matched to and said so contemporaneously (MSG-00113-003). The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00113, weight 1.0, METERED on RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDEPOOL) shows no billing-integrity defect: it reconciles to the cent, the 20.2 km billed matches the 20.18 km trace, erp_gantries is empty, no airport surcharge applies, and a $3.00 pool discount was applied in your favour — nothing is refundable under POL-RD-09(4). Because there is no material deviation, no POL-RD-06 driver-profile check or conduct referral arises, and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 471 completed trips in any event. This is a rider-filed dispute and the result is NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03: the $6.00 contested stays with the driver and payment_status remains CHARGED. Your profile contention is noted and accepted as far as it goes — deviation_claims_60d of 1 is far below the POL-RD-08 threshold and no other profile field was used against you — but it does not change the outcome, which turns entirely on the trace and the matched-itinerary baseline. Confidence is high because nothing decides this case but clean, weight-1.0 instruments; the absent traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00113-01, weight 0.0) is relied on by neither side for the outcome.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the $6.00 contested charge stays in place, and the fare of $26.83 stands.

The baseline. TRP-00113 is a RYDE_POOL booking, so POL-RD-12 fixes the POL-RD-01 baseline at the matched-itinerary distance quoted at match time — trip_record.optimal_distance_km of 19.40 km — and not the 15.80 km solo figure the rider quoted. Both figures sit on EV-TRIP-00113 for comparison. POL-RD-12 says in terms that a claim measured against solo_optimal_distance_km has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground; the 4.4 km the claim contends for is an artefact of that mis-citation. On the facts, the rider was on notice before the wheels turned: the platform's own match notification MSG-00113-001 (18:42:04, read 18:42:31, trip started 18:47:10) states the pooled route includes one Hougang Central pickup at an estimate of 19.4 km / 34 min. The Hougang stop the rider complains of is the platform-matched co-rider collection, and POL-RD-12 excludes co-rider collection and drop-off distance from excess by name.

The measurement. The governing actual figure is the GPS trace, not the bill. EV-GPS-00113 records trace_distance_km of 20.18 km over the run, on 217 fixes at a 10-second cadence with 100% coverage and no gaps — unimpaired, so no POL-RD-07 consequence arises. Against the 19.40 km matched baseline the excess is 0.78 km, or 4.02%. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess exceeds 20% of optimal (3.88 km) AND 0.8 km absolute; 0.78 km clears neither and misses the absolute limb by about 20 metres. No deviation exists, and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. The rider's advocate accepts this arithmetic, and the driver's advocate argues it; the two sides do not actually differ on the outcome.

Remaining points. There is no billing-integrity defect to refund under POL-RD-09(4): erp_gantries is empty, no airport surcharge applies to a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, the line items reconcile to the cent, and the 3.00 pool discount was applied in the rider's favour. POL-RD-06 is not engaged — a 0.78 km excess is nowhere near the 8.0 km / 50% material gate, and in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 471 completed trips, so no repeat-pattern uplift and no driver-conduct referral arises. On the rider's profile, POL-GEN-01 governs: deviation_claims_60d of 1 is far below the four unsubstantiated claims POL-RD-08 requires, so no enhanced corroboration burden attaches to her, and the other fields on that profile (rating, prior_disputes_filed, prior_no_show_flags) are context only and were not used against her.

On the record's two discarded claims: one from each side cited the absent traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00113-01 (weight 0.0) without naming its MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code, and both were discarded on the mechanical disclosure check. Neither affects the result, because no POL-RD-03 closure exoneration is relied on and this case turns on POL-RD-12; a missing artifact can carry no fact.

Confidence. No deciding fact rests on any artifact below weight 1.0; the trace and the trip record that carry the excess finding are both at full weight.

ruling.explanation: Rider and driver: this was a Ryde Pool booking (TRP-00113), and that fact decides the case. Under POL-RD-12 a pooled trip is measured against the matched-itinerary optimal recorded at booking — 19.40 km on the trip record — and NOT against the solo-rider figure of 15.80 km, which the record carries separately for reference only. POL-RD-12 says in terms that a claim measured against the solo figure has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone, so the rider's 20.2 km against 15.8 km comparison cannot be used. Measuring correctly, POL-RD-01 requires the GPS trace figure rather than the rounded 20.2 km on the trip record, and the trace records 20.18 km over an unbroken, unimpaired run (217 fixes, 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps). The excess is therefore 0.78 km, or 4.02% of the matched optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess exceeds BOTH 0.8 km in absolute terms AND 20% of optimal; 0.78 km clears neither, missing the absolute limb by 20 metres. The arithmetic does not support a deviation, and no exculpatory clause needs to be invoked to defeat the claim. The Hougang stop the rider complains of is in any event the matched co-rider pickup, which POL-RD-12 excludes from excess by name: the platform notified the rider at 18:42:04 of 'one pickup at Hougang Central… Estimated 19.4 km, 34 min', the log shows it read at 18:42:31, and the trip did not start until 18:47:10, so the pooled route was disclosed before the wheels turned, and the trace shows the vehicle stationary at that stop. I also ran the billing-integrity check that POL-RD-01 preserves independently of any deviation: the fare is METERED, its lines reconcile to the cent, distance_charged_km of 20.2 is the rounded copy of the 20.18 km trace figure, erp_gantries is empty, the airport surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and a 3.00 pool discount was applied in the rider's favour — so there is no phantom line and nothing to refund under POL-RD-09(4). On the driver's profile, deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 471 completed 90-day trips, so no repeat pattern exists, no POL-RD-06(b) uplift is available and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises; nor does any other POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fire — the trace is unimpaired, the trip identifiers match across the three instruments, the timestamps agree, and no exculpatory clause was invoked against an artifact missing from the pool. The outcome is NO_ACTION: the rider's claim is not supported by the evidence and the $6.00 contested charge stands, with payment_status and refund_issued_sgd left as they are. The two claims (one from each side) that cited the missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00113-01 without naming its MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code were discarded on the mechanical check, as recorded below; their subject matter — the absence of any advisory — was not needed, because this case is decided by POL-RD-12 and not by POL-RD-03. Confidence is high: the deciding facts are carried by the GPS trace and the trip record, both at weight 1.0, and no artifact below full weight supports the ruling.

The rider's 15.8 km figure is trip_record.solo_optimal_distance_km, carried on the record for reference only. Under POL-RD-12 a claim that measures excess against solo_optimal_distance_km has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone. The 4.4 km shortfall the claim_text asserts (20.2 minus 15.8) is an artefact of that mis-citation, not of anything the driver did. Both figures are on EV-TRIP-00113 and the ruling should name them side by side so it is visible why the arithmetic changes.

The detour the rider complains of — 'the driver went off to Hougang' — is the matched co-rider pickup, and POL-RD-12 excludes it by name: distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary is never a deviation and is removed from excess before POL-RD-01 is applied. The trace shows the vehicle stationary at Hougang Central for the boarding stop, consistent with a pick-up rather than a wander.

The rider was on notice before the wheels turned, so this is not a case of a route being altered behind his back. The platform's own match notification MSG-00113-001, sent 18:42:04, states 'Your pooled route now includes one pickup at Hougang Central before your drop-off. Estimated 19.4 km, 34 min'; the log records it read at 18:42:31, and the trip did not start until 18:47:10. The 19.4 km matched-itinerary figure on the trip record is the same figure the rider was quoted in the app.

The driver's counterparty statement is corroborated rather than contradicted by the platform's own records: he says a second passenger was matched at Hougang and that he drove the app route, and the system notification MSG-00113-001 records that match, MSG-00113-003 records his contemporaneous explanation 'pool booking, picking up the other passenger, app route', and the trace shows the stop. Nothing in the admitted evidence shows the vehicle anywhere the matched pooled itinerary did not put it.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. The trace here is unimpaired: 217 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 and a 10 s sampling interval — so there is no gap, jump or sampling defect under POL-RD-07. What that clean trace shows is 0.78 km and 4.02%. The threshold is not met, the burden never shifts to the driver, and no exculpatory clause need be invoked to defeat the claim.

No driver_profile check is engaged on this trip. POL-RD-06 is consulted only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation, and a 0.78 km excess is far below the 8.0 km / 50% material gate. In any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 471, so there is no repeat-deviation pattern, no POL-RD-06(b) FULL_REFUND uplift is available, and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is justified.

No traffic advisory covers the Punggol, Hougang or CTE corridors in this window — EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING and carries weight 0.0 — and the driver does not need one.
